title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space sector is buzzing with activity, from satellite launches to new funding rounds. Meanwhile, the military's interest in space resilience continues to grow, as traditional boundaries blur between defense and commercial ventures.

themes.title: Satellite Launches Galore
themes.body: The upcoming Ariane 6 mission is set to deploy 36 Amazon Leo satellites, showcasing the increasing demand for low Earth orbit capabilities. Meanwhile, the Qianfan constellation has reached a milestone of 200 satellites, highlighting China's rapid advancements in space infrastructure.

themes.title: Funding and Valuations Rising
themes.body: Apex's valuation has soared to $2.3 billion following a substantial funding round, reflecting investor confidence in the satellite manufacturing sector. Similarly, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round indicates a robust appetite for innovative space solutions.

themes.title: Defense Meets Commercial Space
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical satellite constellation bid, blurring the lines between commercial and defense applications in space. This trend is further echoed by the Defense-Tech IPO window showing signs of life, as companies seek to capitalize on the growing intersection of these sectors.

themes.title: Moon Bases and Mars Dreams
themes.body: While discussions about building a moon base gain traction, experts caution against losing focus on Mars exploration. Balancing these ambitions will be crucial as agencies and private players navigate the complexities of interplanetary aspirations.
